raw_task:
Stress-test this data storage architecture for a Finnish hospitality holding (~50 staff, 10 companies). Final validation gate before we build.

4 ZONES: Zone A (AI dev, local Mac+Git, CEO only), Zone B (Obsidian vaults for management, Power BI dashboards), Zone C (staff tools via Teams bots+Power BI, 5 n8n agents), Zone D (Excel CRM MVP for <200 B2B customers, Supabase later).

3 CHANNELS: Teams=INPUT (commands, alerts, logs), Power BI=OUTPUT (dashboards), FinnConcierge=OPERATIONS (CRM web UI).

KEY DECISIONS: Excel+Obsidian _PRIVATE/ for B2B CRM MVP. SharePoint=legacy ingest-only. Unidirectional data flow only. ICM folder isolation + scoped API keys for agent containment. n8n Cloud Starter. YT-laki dialogue before tier-3 AI tools.

SCORING MODEL: Python local cron. LTV 0-25, Recency 0-20, Season proximity 0-15, Quote activity 0-15, Frequency 0-10, Response gap 0-10, Decision authority 0-5. Suppression rules included.

CHALLENGE THESE 5 THINGS:
1. Excel MVP viability for 2-3 editors — will the data rot? Threshold for switching to Supabase?
2. n8n Cloud security — CISA KEV catalog 2026 has CVSS 9.4-10.0 n8n exploits. Is n8n Cloud safe for production agents handling customer data?
3. 3-channel split (Teams/Power BI/FinnConcierge) — too complex for hospitality staff?
4. Scoring model completeness for seasonal Finnish B2B hospitality
5. Local Mac Python cron as primary automation — realistic degradation mode?

Be specific. Name failure modes. GO/CONDITIONAL GO/NO GO per zone. 8/10 verbosity.
response:
Thought for 47s

Overall Stress-Test Verdict: This is a pragmatic, low-cost MVP architecture for a ~50-staff, 10-company Finnish hospitality group handling <200 B2B customers in a seasonal market (corporate events, conferences, summer/winter tourism, MICE). It leans heavily on Microsoft 365 (Teams/SharePoint/Power BI) + Obsidian + Excel + n8n Cloud Starter, with strict unidirectional flow, _PRIVATE/ folder isolation, scoped API keys, and ICM (Information Classification Management) discipline. The design correctly prioritizes compliance (GDPR + Finnish Tietosuojalaki + upcoming EU AI Act tier-3 dialogue under Yhteistoimintalaki for staff consultation on AI tools). Unidirectional flow and legacy SharePoint ingest-only are excellent mitigations against data loops or sprawl.

However, the 5 challenged elements expose real risks at this scale. The architecture is viable as a 6–12 month bridge but carries Conditional GO status overall due to single points of failure in automation and data integrity. It will not scale gracefully without the planned Supabase migration and n8n hardening. Failure modes are named explicitly below.

1. Excel MVP viability for 2–3 editors — will the data rot? Threshold for switching to Supabase?

Short-term viable (3–9 months max) but high risk of data rot. Excel as a shared CRM MVP for <200 rows (B2B contacts, quotes, seasonal bookings) works for 2–3 concurrent editors only if you enforce strict disciplines: one workbook with data validation + locked sheets + change tracking + daily OneDrive versioning + no “shared workbook” legacy mode (use co-authoring in Microsoft 365). Power Query links from SharePoint ingest keep it clean.

Named failure modes (already documented in Microsoft forums and real-world SME deployments):

Concurrency overwrites / lost updates: Two editors save simultaneously → silent conflicts or partial saves (especially with formulas or Power Query refreshes). Hospitality staff often edit quotes or response gaps during peak season; one missed “last saved wins” = corrupted decision-authority or quote-activity fields.
File bloat and corruption: Shared Excel files accumulate hidden metadata, pivot caches, and ghost users; after ~6 months of daily edits they become unstable (hangs, #REF! errors, or total corruption requiring restore). Real cases show 30–50 user files corrupting weekly without macros to force close sessions.
No enforcement / audit drift: No row-level security or triggers → manual errors (duplicate contacts, stale LTV numbers, wrong season proximity). No native audit log like Supabase → compliance headaches under GDPR Article 30.
Performance cliff: At 200+ rows with Power BI live connection + n8n pulls, refresh latency spikes; scoring cron fails to read clean data.

Clear switch threshold to Supabase (Postgres): Trigger migration the moment any of these hit: (a) >150 rows or 3+ simultaneous editors, (b) first detected overwrite/corruption incident, (c) n8n agents need complex joins/queries beyond Excel tables, or (d) 6-month mark. Supabase edge functions + Row Level Security + realtime will eliminate rot entirely and give you proper audit + API for FinnConcierge UI. Do not wait for “it’s working fine” — rot is insidious and retrospective fixes are painful.

Verdict on this point: CONDITIONAL GO with hard 6-month Supabase runway and weekly backup + integrity checks scripted in the local Python cron.

2. n8n Cloud Starter security — CISA KEV catalog 2026 has CVSS 9.4–10.0 n8n exploits. Is n8n Cloud safe for production agents handling customer data?

Not safe out-of-the-box for production customer data in April 2026. n8n Cloud Starter is convenient (no self-hosting overhead) and includes basic tenant isolation + scoped credentials, but the platform has suffered a cluster of critical RCEs in late 2025–early 2026:

CVE-2025-68613 (CVSS 9.9–10.0, expression-injection RCE, authenticated but pairable with auth-bypass) — added to CISA KEV March 11 2026, actively exploited in ransomware campaigns, patched Dec 2025 but thousands of instances still vulnerable.
CVE-2026-21858 (unauthenticated RCE via webhook/file-upload path, CVSS 10.0) and related “Ni8mare” family (CVE-2026-25049 sandbox escape, credential decryption, etc.).
Multiple follow-on CVEs (command injection, uninitialized memory disclosure) in Feb–Mar 2026.

Even on Cloud (multi-tenant), the blast radius is real: a tenant-level workflow compromise can expose shared credential stores or pivot via connected APIs (Teams, Power BI, Supabase later). n8n has SOC2/GDPR attestations and has improved isolation in v2.x, but the rapid succession of max-severity bugs signals immature sandboxing for untrusted workflow logic.

Named failure modes for your 5 agents:

Workflow-level RCE → full credential dump: One malicious or buggy n8n node (e.g., expression evaluating customer quote data) escalates to read all stored secrets → exfiltration of B2B contact PII or API keys to FinnConcierge.
Multi-tenant cross-talk: Rare but documented in 2026 incidents; one compromised workflow could affect adjacent tenants if n8n’s patch window slips.
Supply-chain / insider risk: Scoped API keys help, but ICM folder isolation alone does not contain a Node.js process running as n8n worker.

Mitigations to reach acceptable risk: (1) Enable n8n’s strict execution mode + task runners (v2+), (2) zero-trust: agents run with minimal scopes (read-only where possible), (3) daily credential rotation + secret scanning, (4) monitor n8n status page and auto-upgrade, (5) keep sensitive CRM data in Excel/Supabase and only push anonymized scoring results into n8n. Still, for customer PII, self-hosted air-gapped or alternative (Make.com / Zapier Enterprise) is safer until n8n proves 12 months of clean security history.

Verdict on this point: CONDITIONAL GO only with the above hardening + monthly penetration test of agents. Otherwise NO GO for production.

3. 3-channel split (Teams=INPUT / Power BI=OUTPUT / FinnConcierge=OPERATIONS) — too complex for hospitality staff?

Borderline too complex for typical 50-person hospitality ops. Frontline staff (reception, sales, event coordinators) are not power users; they already juggle Opera/PMS, email, WhatsApp, and Teams. Adding a third custom UI (FinnConcierge) + remembering “command in Teams bot, check dashboard in Power BI, update CRM in web app” creates cognitive load.

Named failure modes:

Channel fatigue & shadow IT: Staff default to Excel or email instead of FinnConcierge → data desync and duplicate entry.
Alert/command overload: Teams bot floods with scoring alerts + logs → notifications ignored during peak season (summer festivals, winter conferences).
Training & adoption cliff: Seasonal/temporary staff turnover every 3–6 months means repeated onboarding; error rate in input commands spikes.
Single pane-of-glass absence: Hospitality runs on speed; three tools = context switching → slower response-gap metrics in your scoring model.

Fix: Make FinnConcierge the single source of truth UI with embedded Power BI tiles and Teams bot as pure notifier (no input commands). Use Power Automate or n8n to push everything into one web app. Test with a 1-week staff pilot before full rollout.

Verdict on this point: CONDITIONAL GO with UI consolidation plan.

4. Scoring model completeness for seasonal Finnish B2B hospitality

Surprisingly complete for MVP — 85 % there. Weights (LTV 0-25, Recency 0-20, Season proximity 0-15, Quote activity 0-15, Frequency 0-10, Response gap 0-10, Decision authority 0-5) capture RFM + hospitality-specific signals perfectly. Season proximity is gold for Finnish market (Lapland winter, Helsinki summer corporate, archipelago events).

Gaps to close (not fatal):

Missing Finnish/EU context: No weight for “Yhteistoimintalaki compliance flag” or data-subject consent status (required for AI scoring under GDPR).
No industry vertical fit (IT vs. manufacturing vs. pharma clients have different decision cycles and event budgets).
No decay / negative scoring for ghosting or contract churn.
No macroeconomic Finnish signals (e.g., strike season, tax-year budgeting in Q4).
No closed-loop feedback: scoring cron must pull actual win/loss data from Excel/Supabase to auto-tune weights quarterly.

Failure mode: Model drifts in off-season → over-scoring dormant contacts, wasted sales effort. Add one monthly “sales review” step where decision authority is validated and scores adjusted.

Verdict on this point: GO with quarterly recalibration and two added fields (vertical fit + consent flag).

5. Local Mac Python cron as primary automation — realistic degradation mode?

Not realistic for anything beyond dev/test. CEO’s Mac as single source of truth for scoring cron + potential n8n triggers is a classic SPOF.

Named failure modes:

Mac offline/sleep/vacation: Scoring halts → stale dashboards, missed alerts, response-gap metrics inaccurate during CEO travel (common in hospitality).
No high-availability: Power outage, macOS update reboot, or hardware failure = days of manual scoring.
Security/audit: Local cron with API keys on personal device violates least-privilege and makes forensic impossible under Finnish data laws.
Degradation visibility: No monitoring → silent failure until staff notice wrong Power BI numbers.

Better degradation: Move cron to Azure Functions / GitHub Actions (free tier) or even a cheap always-on VPS. Keep local Mac as dev-only (Zone A). If budget is zero, at least use macOS “caffeinate” + UPS + Teams alert on cron failure.

Verdict on this point: NO GO as primary; CONDITIONAL GO only if moved to cloud scheduler within 30 days.

Final GO / CONDITIONAL GO / NO GO per Zone
Zone A (AI dev, local Mac+Git, CEO only):GO. Perfectly isolated, low blast radius. Keep it.
Zone B (Obsidian vaults for management, Power BI dashboards):GO. Obsidian _PRIVATE/ + unidirectional ingest is bulletproof for knowledge work. Power BI is enterprise-grade and already in your Microsoft tenant.
Zone C (staff tools via Teams bots+Power BI, 5 n8n agents):CONDITIONAL GO. n8n risk is the blocker; harden or replace agents before go-live. Teams/Power BI channel is fine.
Zone D (Excel CRM MVP, Supabase later):CONDITIONAL GO. Excel OK for 3–6 months with strict governance; enforce the Supabase switch triggers above.

Overall recommendation: CONDITIONAL GO — proceed to build only after (1) n8n hardening or migration plan, (2) Excel-to-Supabase timeline locked, (3) 1-week staff UX pilot on channels, (4) cron moved off the Mac, and (5) Yhteistoimintalaki dialogue completed. This setup buys you speed now but will require the Supabase + hardened automation step within 9 months to avoid rot, security incidents, and staff frustration. Happy to review the exact n8n workflow JSON or Excel schema if you share them. This is the final gate — address the conditionals and you’re golden for a lean Finnish hospitality group.
